testimonials.text: The integration of blast physics with clinical care, especially how understanding overpressure waves directly explains the injury patterns we see in the lungs, bowel, and ear.
Thoroughly enjoyable. A former Royal Navy Medic, we did learn about blast injuries but this really added greater depth of understanding to injuries, initial treatment and follow up treatment.
I found the information about acute management of blast injury extremely interesting.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning how blast injuries are classified and managed, especially the differences between primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary injuries. I also found the emergency management of blast injuries in pediatric and pregnant patients particularly interesting.
Paediatric resuscitation from blast injury. Not something I ever thought we would see in the U.K. but it has now happened and we must be prepped.
